newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks seen testing 6-yr highs on Dow jump.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks seen testing 6-yr highs on Dow jump.

text.p: Taiwan share prices are expected to open stronger and test six-year highs on Tuesday following Wall Street's sharp rise overnight, brokers said.
The index is expected to challenge a six-year peak of 8,655.82 set on April 9 and possibly break the 8,700 level due to a lack of bearish factors, brokers said.
"It will definitely challenge another new high, especially because of the rise on Wall Street," said David Yu, vice president of International Investment Trust.
Electronics shares, hit recently by U.S. allegations that Taiwan had dumped memory chips in the United States, should be the main beneficiary of Wall Street's strength, brokers said.
On Monday the index finished 151.48 points, or 1.78 percent, higher at 8,639.37. Turnover was a heavy T$166.68 billion.
A 8,600-8,750 range was tipped for Tuesday.
In New York, the Dow Jones industrial average closed up 60.21 points at 6,451.90, its largest gain since a 101-point surge on March 24. -- Kevin Chen (5080815)
